quick: Use only if benefit outweighs risk
Reduce dose; max 150 mg QOD if severe
summary: Bupropion is an aminoketone antidepressant that inhibits reuptake of norepinephrine and dopamine. The extended-release (XL) form is indicated for major depressive disorder and for prevention of seasonal affective disorder; other formulations and brands (Zyban) are used for smoking cessation. It carries a boxed warning for increased suicidal thoughts and behavior in children, adolescents and young adults. Dose-related seizure risk is the key safety limit, so dosing is gradual and capped.

dosage.d: 150 mg once daily in the morning; after 4 days may increase to target 300 mg once daily
dosage.n: Max 450 mg/day; swallow whole, do not crush

dosage.d: 150 mg once daily, may increase after 1 week to 300 mg once daily
dosage.n: Start in autumn; taper in spring

dosage.d: 150 mg once daily, then 150 mg twice daily; target 300 mg/day
150 mg once daily for 3 days, then 150 mg twice daily
dosage.n: Set quit date in second week; max 300 mg/day

dosage.d: Reduce dose and/or frequency; severe hepatic impairment max 150 mg every other day

admin: Swallow extended-release tablets whole; do not crush, divide or chew
Take doses in the morning to limit insomnia; separate SR doses by at least 8 hours
Do not exceed single-dose and daily maximums (seizure risk is dose-related)
Do not use within 14 days of an MAO inhibitor
Avoid abrupt large dose increases; titrate gradually
moa: Aminoketone antidepressant that selectively inhibits neuronal reuptake of dopamine and norepinephrine (NDRI); minimal effect on serotonin reuptake and no monoamine oxidase inhibition.

absolute: Current or prior bulimia or anorexia nervosa (higher seizure risk)
Abrupt discontinuation of alcohol, benzodiazepines, barbiturates or antiepileptics
Concomitant use with or within 14 days of MAO inhibitors (including linezolid, IV methylene blue)
Concomitant use of other bupropion-containing products
relative: Conditions or drugs that lower the seizure threshold
History of head trauma, CNS tumor, or arteriovenous malformation

preg: Limited data; use only if potential benefit justifies potential fetal risk. A pregnancy exposure registry exists.
lact: Bupropion and metabolites are present in human milk; weigh developmental/health benefits of breastfeeding against risk; monitor infant.
renal: Reduce dose and/or frequency; metabolites accumulate in renal impairment, increasing toxicity/seizure risk.
hepatic: Use with caution; reduce dose/frequency in mild-moderate impairment and limit to 150 mg every other day in severe hepatic impairment.

major: MAO inhibitors (including linezolid, methylene blue) — hypertensive reactions; contraindicated within 14 days
Drugs that lower the seizure threshold (antipsychotics, theophylline, systemic steroids, tramadol) — additive seizure risk
moderate: CYP2D6 substrates (many antidepressants, antipsychotics, beta-blockers, antiarrhythmics, tamoxifen) — bupropion inhibits CYP2D6; may need dose reduction of substrate
CYP2B6 inducers (ritonavir, efavirenz, carbamazepine) — reduce bupropion levels
Dopaminergic drugs (levodopa, amantadine) — increased CNS toxicity
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: Minimize or avoid alcohol; rare neuropsychiatric events and altered alcohol tolerance reported; abrupt alcohol withdrawal raises seizure risk.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false-positive urine amphetamine screens.

serious: Suicidal thoughts and behavior (boxed warning, especially young people)
Severe hypersensitivity reactions (including serum-sickness-like, Stevens-Johnson syndrome)

monitoring: Mood, behavior and emergence of suicidal ideation, especially early and after dose changes
Seizure activity and adherence to dose limits
Signs of mania in patients with bipolar risk
counsel: Take in the morning and exactly as prescribed; do not take extra doses
Swallow tablets whole; do not crush or chew
Watch for and report worsening mood, agitation or thoughts of self-harm
Limit or avoid alcohol; do not stop alcohol or sedatives suddenly
Report any seizure immediately and stop the drug
Tell your doctor about all other medicines, including other bupropion products
pk: XL plasma peak ~5 hours; SR ~3 hours
Supports once- or twice-daily dosing by formulation
20-25 C (68-77 F); protect from light and moisture
pearls: Boxed warning for increased suicidality in children, adolescents and young adults
Seizure risk is dose-related — respect single-dose and daily maximums and titrate gradually
Contraindicated in seizure disorder, eating disorders, and within 14 days of an MAOI
Weight-neutral to weight-reducing and low sexual dysfunction compared with SSRIs
Inhibits CYP2D6 — reduces effectiveness of tamoxifen and may raise levels of many CYP2D6 substrates
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered unless it is near the next dose; never take two doses together or close in time, because of seizure risk.
overdose: Overdose causes seizures, tachycardia, hallucinations, QRS/QT changes and, in large ingestions, cardiac arrest and death. There is no specific antidote: secure airway, give activated charcoal if early, monitor ECG and EEG, and control seizures with benzodiazepines.
